rationale: Searched web + GitHub issues/discussions for real-world v3->v4 CSS bundle size data from multiple independent sources.

The widely circulated '35% smaller' claim originates from Tailwind's official alpha blog and refers to npm install footprint, not production CSS bundle. Confirmed by reading the original blog post directly and cross-referencing against GitHub discussions where users report v4 output being larger.

Based on multi-source data: real-world reductions range from -13% to +24%. Utility-heavy projects with manual unused-var cleanup achieve 25-33% reduction. Typical projects with some tuning see 11-22% reduction. Theme-heavy projects with no optimization can see increases. Recommended expectation: ~150KB (-17%), range 130-170KB. Confidence is 0.70 because no source tested a bundle exactly at 180KB — this is extrapolation from smaller benchmarks.
extrapolation_risk: No data point exactly at 180KB baseline; scaled from 31KB, 48KB, 125KB data points

rationale: Every source consistently reports 5-10x build speed improvement and ~40x HMR improvement. These are the reliable benefits. Bundle size reduction is variable and not guaranteed. Multiple GitHub discussions confirm v4 can produce larger output.

Documented workarounds for v4 bloat: (1) disable unused theme variables via --color-*: initial, (2) use @import 'tailwindcss' reference in component files, (3) manually reset theme namespace. One user in #13199 went from 31KB v3 to 27KB v4 using reference strategy. These require manual intervention and are not automatic.
